hypothesis: Very low/reduced switch stress necessarily requires more active switches or extra magnetic cores
supporting_evidence: some active-clamp designs do add auxiliary devices
counterevidence: 0028 reaches 0.1375 with one active switch; OJPEL 2025 counterexample achieves soft switching with no extra active switch/magnetic core in the snubber
authorized_statement: No universal active-device penalty is supported
prohibited_statement: Do not claim low stress/soft switching inherently requires additional active switches or magnetic cores

hypothesis: Soft switching is necessary to achieve low normalized main-switch stress
supporting_evidence: 0024/0028/0030 combine soft switching and reduced stress
counterevidence: 0027 has measured normalized switch stress 0.155 while its comparison status is no soft switching
authorized_statement: Low switch stress can be achieved with or without soft switching in current evidence
prohibited_statement: Do not treat ZVS/ZCS as a prerequisite for low stress

hypothesis: Reducing main-switch stress tends to redistribute design burden into passive count, magnetic design, diode stress, or integration constraints
supporting_evidence: 0027 uses 1/8/8/1 switch/diode/cap/core structure and explicitly links added diodes/caps to gain/stress; 0028 has main stress 0.1375 but max diode stress 0.60 and uses input inductor + TWCI; 0024 uses separate input inductor + CI; review literature treats component/magnetic/input-ripple tradeoffs as first-class
counterevidence: counter-search finds designs reducing some penalties; 0030 structural data incomplete; no universal monotonic relationship demonstrated
authorized_statement: Current evidence supports investigating burden redistribution across device/passive/magnetic dimensions
prohibited_statement: Do not call this a universal law or Research Gap
next_gate: resolve 0030 structure; add direct-scale counterexamples; independent extraction; snowball citations

hypothesis: Soft switching enables higher switching frequency without efficiency penalty
supporting_evidence: soft-switched records span 50-100 kHz with useful efficiency descriptors
counterevidence: auxiliary/thermal/measurement boundaries differ; 0027 hard-switched at 50 kHz; no controlled frequency experiment across independent papers
authorized_statement: Frequency and switching mode must remain covariates
prohibited_statement: Do not attribute efficiency differences to soft switching or fs alone

hypothesis: Common ground + continuous input current + very low normalized stress (<0.25) is an unresolved three-way design constraint
supporting_evidence: current L5 records have incomplete common-ground/input-ripple coverage; 0027 common ground is no
counterevidence: OJPEL 2025 provides common ground + continuous input + soft switching but stress ~0.40; other recent candidates may enter <0.25 region after audit
authorized_statement: This is a useful targeted search question only
prohibited_statement: Do not label it a gap or impossibility
next_gate: target direct-scale records with all three fields measured/text-locked
